newsitem.title: australia: Defence lawyer quits Australia mass murder case.
newsitem.headline: Defence lawyer quits Australia mass murder case.

text.p: The defence lawyer for the man charged with Australia's worst mass murder in modern times has resigned from the case.
"Media reports that I no longer represent Martin Bryant are correct," David Gunson said in a statement issued on Wednesday, two days after Bryant, 29, pleaded not guilty to 35 murders.
"I will make no further comment as to the reasons or circumstances surrounding this development," Gunson added.

The statement confirms local newspaper reports that another lawyer was considering defending Bryant, who is accused of murdering 35 people in a shooting spree on April 28 at the historic Port Arthur convict site in the southern island state of Tasmania.
The media reports named Hobart lawyer John Avery as Gunson's likely replacement, but Avery was not immediately available for comment.
Bryant's case is due in court again on Friday for a trial date to be set. It is expected the trial will start on November 19.
